current_row.boundary_rationale: The opening verse of this unit is web:Isa.42.18, “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.”, pointed הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte), a fresh imperative address to the deaf and blind, distinct from the third-person idol-trusters closing the previous span. A parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.42.17, immediately before this unit's own onset. The addressee is named at web:Isa.42.19, “Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as Yahweh’s servant?”, pointed מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּ֣י אִם עַבְדִּ֔י וְחֵרֵ֖שׁ כְּמַלְאָכִ֣י אֶשְׁלָ֑ח מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּמְשֻׁלָּ֔ם וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte), identified by the common noun servant without further identifying the referent. It closes at web:Isa.42.25. A parashah PE mark (single-witness) closes at oshb:Isa.42.25, corroborating the break.

current_row.device_notes: The closing verse reads in full, web:Isa.42.25, “Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle. It set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know. It burned him, but he didn’t take it to heart.”, pointed וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ חֵמָ֣ה אַפּ֔וֹ וֶעֱז֖וּז מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא יָשִׂ֥ים עַל לֵֽב (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte). The servant addressed here is named by the common noun 'my servant' and by 'Yahweh's servant' at web:Isa.42.19, a spare designation this row does not expand; whether this figure is the same one presented at web:Isa.42.1 or a distinct referent is a held question this row does not settle. A ketiv/qere note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.42.20, inside this span; a second ketiv/qere note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.42.24; both are disclosed here without adjudicating either specific reading. This span's own bytes name a party in a different role: יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, tier: byte) names Jacob and Israel as the ones given up to plunder; that naming is disclosed neutrally here, held open against the servant designation of web:Isa.42.19 and not resolved in either direction. This unit's own opening seam is straddled by the blindness lexeme: the clause וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, tier: byte) reaches into this unit's own onset, its own עִוְרִ֗ים re-collating against וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte) at accent_stripped tier and continuing at עִוֵּר֙ (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte) (sweep: 5 verses, the blind lexeme in chs 42-43: oshb:Isa.42.7, 42.16, 42.18, 42.19, 43.8). The close seam is a cross-part seam and carries two further devices: וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) is answered by וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte), the two sharing only the fire-verb stem, the attested tokens returning tier NONE; and the same name-pair recurs at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte), likewise stem-level against oshb:Isa.42.24.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways from bytes. Parashah inventory (single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets, never a driver): MT 42:25 carries PE and MT 42:17 SAMEKH, so the mark claims are type-correct. The shipped boundary field's entire close argument is the PE sentence, and a programmatic scan of every field of the row finds no koh-amar formula anywhere (no skeleton כה אמר (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: skeleton), no 'says'); the row's only engagement with oshb:Isa.43.1 is the name-pair continuity device בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) in device_notes, read stem-level against יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, tier: byte), which argues cohesion across the close seam rather than a break. The signal that carries the seam is the divine-frame onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte); skeleton sweep of the formula: 48 verses book-wide, exactly 4 in chs 41-43 (oshb:Isa.42.5, oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.14, oshb:Isa.43.16), all divine-owned since the four royal-messenger sites are confined to chs 36-37 (36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) -- the auditor's digits hold. Tested the other way: nothing in the shipped row supplies a tier-1 close warrant that the auditor missed. Severity: the seam location is byte-sound and the PE claim is byte-true, so there is no load-bearing boundary defect and no byte-false load-bearing claim (not high); a close warranted only by a tier-3 mark that 'corroborates' an unnamed break is a defective warrant not alone load-bearing, and it is more than a disclosure slip because the seam-carrying signal is absent from the record (not low). Medium as filed.

readjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes at MT 42:25|43:1, both sides. The row's own close: וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא יָשִׂ֥ים עַל לֵֽב (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) is third-person narration of the poured-out wrath, its runs at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no closing formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant; the PE at MT 42:25 (single-witness inventory: SAMEKH 42:17, PE 42:25) is tier-3 corroboration, never a driver. Following unit's onset: וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) is the divine-owned messenger formula, the ruled formula-onset class (§2a); the koh-amar skeleton stands at 48 verses book-wide and at exactly 4 in chs 41-43 (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier: MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16), all divine-owned since the royal-messenger sites are confined to MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16 and 37:3, and the verse-initial three-token onset is unique (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier). So the rear seam is warranted from the following unit's onset. The row as shipped: its entire close sentence is the PE, a programmatic skeleton scan of every field finds no koh-amar formula anywhere in the row, and its only engagement with MT 43:1 is the name-pair thread בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) in device_notes, read stem-level against יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, tier: byte), which argues cohesion across the seam rather than a break. The filed finding already weighed both sides (the row's close and the next unit's onset); the complete test re-derives it unchanged and agrees with the prior adjudication's rule. Seam location byte-sound, mark claim byte-true, the seam-carrying signal absent from the record: confirm medium; field repair as proposed, no span change.

items.adjudicator_grounds: The rejected-alternative sentence is as the auditor quotes it: its sole refusal ground is an absence-of-form claim keyed to web:Isa.42.21 with no pointed splice and no tier, and its only extent statement is 'through to the chapter's close'. Bytes: יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר (oshb:Isa.42.21, tier: byte) opens on the divine name as grammatical subject, its verbs carry the prefix-conjugation yod of third-person forms, and it has no vocative, no imperative and no speech frame -- skeleton sweep of the koh-amar formula places no site between oshb:Isa.42.5 and oshb:Isa.43.1 -- so the form claim is true and the rival rightly refused; the translation witness corroborates the absence, “It pleased Yahweh, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law and make it honorable.” (web:Isa.42.21), a third-person statement. Tested the other way: the finding is not overreach, because form-class labels are byte-checkable claims under the tier-disclosure standard and pointed splices are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, and this one is the strongest rival's only ground; and in a row whose close carries no tier-1 warrant the chapter-keyed extent clause is the row's sole statement of where the unit ends, tier-4 metadata standing in for an argument. True claim, rightly refused rival, wrong evidencing: defective warrant not alone load-bearing (not high, the boundary is sound; not low, it is the only ground for the strongest rival plus a tier-4 extent). Medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens a fresh salvation oracle at the divine-frame onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- one of four divine-owned koh-amar frames in this run of oracles, alongside כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier) earlier in the sequence (sweep: 4 verses, the koh-amar formula within chs 41-43 -- oshb:Isa.42.5, oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.14, oshb:Isa.43.16, all four divine-owned) -- “But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says:” “Don't be afraid, for I have redeemed you.” (web:Isa.43.1), pairing the creation verbs on the pointed page as בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- Jacob and Israel named as the addressee here, not read as the servant of a trial speech. The fear-not formula repeats at “Don't be afraid, for I am with you.” (web:Isa.43.5) inside the same address, and the unit closes on the matching triad “everyone who is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.” (web:Isa.43.7), spliced at בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף עֲשִׂיתִֽיו (oshb:Isa.43.7, byte tier): the created/formed/made sequence answers the opening pair and closes the unit ahead of the blind-people summons that opens web:Isa.43.8, the gathered-nations address itself not opening until web:Isa.43.9.

items.proposed_change: Reconcile the two rows' stated grounds for the 43:7|43:8 seam so the blind-word tie is described the same way on both sides -- a backward lexical echo carried by a verse that nonetheless opens the following unit -- without moving the seam.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Byte tie verified: עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte) re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.42.19, where it stands inside וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte), and at NONE against oshb:Isa.43.9; a pointed-form sweep of that exact token returns exactly 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (oshb:Isa.42.19, oshb:Isa.43.8), so the backward echo is real and exclusive. The incoherence is in the record, not the seam: this row's refusal clause says the 43:8 summons reaches 'back rather than forward into the nations' gathering', while the neighbor row that opens at 43:8 grounds its onset on that same directive הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte) 'turning into' כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, tier: byte). One row denies the forward affinity the other's onset depends on. Tested the other way: the two rows are reconcilable only by rewording (a backward lexical echo carried by a verse that nonetheless opens the next unit), not as shipped; and both keep the 43:7|43:8 cut, with no parashah mark at MT 43:7 and SAMEKH only at MT 43:10 and 43:13 (single-witness, tier-3), so no span moves and nothing load-bearing fails (not high). A seam pair that characterizes the shared onset verse's affinity in opposite directions inside its load-bearing fields is a defective warrant not alone load-bearing, not a mechanical shortfall (not low). Medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A byte-visible participant shift opens the row: the first-person divine speech that closes Isa.43.7 gives way to a directive naming a third party, הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, byte tier) -- a directive reading, since no per-token parsing layer is staged to fix an imperative or vocative shape at this verse -- “Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.” (oshb:Isa.43.8), turning into the nations-summons כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, byte tier), “Let all the nations be gathered together...Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified” (oshb:Isa.43.9) and the courtroom verdict “"You are my witnesses," says Yahweh” (oshb:Isa.43.10), spliced at אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.10, byte tier). The same verse also names “my servant whom I have chosen” (web:Isa.43.10) in the same breath as the witness verdict; the byte census leaves that servant figure unnamed here, so the row treats the phrase as the addressed ‘you’ of the witness clause rather than deciding it is Israel. The self-declaration “I myself am Yahweh. Besides me, there is no savior.” (web:Isa.43.11) carries through to the close “Yes, since the day was, I am he.” (web:Isa.43.13), spliced at גַּם מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.43.13, byte tier), ahead of the fresh koh-amar frame naming the Redeemer at web:Isa.43.14.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading folds the row into the fear-not oracle preceding it as one extended first-person address, treating the witness-summons of Isa.43.9 as a turn rather than a fresh trial frame.

items.claim: Three curly-quoted WEB English runs are bound to oshb: (MT) refs in the load-bearing boundary field.
items.proposed_change: Re-key the three English runs to web:Isa.43.8, web:Isa.43.9 and web:Isa.43.10, and restore WEB's curly inner quotation marks in the web:Isa.43.10 run.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Witness re-check: the three curly runs are verbatim WEB after punctuation normalization at web:Isa.43.8 (“Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.” is the whole verse), web:Isa.43.9 (ellipsis-aware) and web:Isa.43.10, while the MT bytes the row binds them to -- הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte), כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, tier: byte), אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.10, tier: byte) -- carry no English, so each '(oshb:...)' after an English run names the wrong witness. WEB sets the 43:10 inner quotation in curly marks, “You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh (web:Isa.43.10), and the row's run replaces them with straight ASCII marks, so that run is not character-verbatim as shipped. Tested the other way: the staged quote checker returns GREEN on this row, but only because it binds each curly run to any web: ref within 200 characters with one-verse slack -- the 43:9 and 43:10 runs pass against the later web:Isa.43.10 citation and the 43:8 run is never checked at all -- so the misattribution is real and invisible to the suite, which is the auditor's point, not a refutation. Three false witness bindings in the load-bearing field plus one non-verbatim run, with no boundary claim turning on the witness label: defective citation claims not alone load-bearing (not high; not low, since a wrong witness on a quotation is a false claim, not a missing tag). Medium as filed.

items.claim: The strongest-rejected-alternative field states the rival and records no ground for rejecting it.
items.proposed_change: Add the refusal ground to the field -- the participant change at oshb:Isa.43.8 against the addressed second person running through oshb:Isa.43.1-43.7 -- keeping the field within its one-sentence limit.
items.adjudicator_grounds: The field reads exactly as quoted and ends without any refusal clause; the rival it names, folding the row into the preceding fear-not oracle, is the row's strongest and is answered nowhere in the field. The only onset ground in the row is the participant shift at הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte), which the row itself hedges for want of a morphology layer; from the bytes the shift is visible whichever way the opening verb is read (perfect or imperative), since the first-person creator speech closing on בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף עֲשִׂיתִֽיו (oshb:Isa.43.7, tier: byte) gives way to a third-party object, a blind people with eyes, and then to the nations summons כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, tier: byte) -- so a one-clause refusal was available and the auditor's proposed ground is byte-supportable, with one caveat for the docket: 43:7 itself already carries third-person suffixes on the triad, so 'second person running through 43:1-43:7' should be worded to the verse where the address is second person. One correction to the finding's ancillary claim: only the preceding neighbor carries an explicit refusal clause; the following neighbor's field likewise states its rival's case without refusing it, so 'neighbor rows on both sides' is half wrong -- immaterial to this item. No parashah mark sits at MT 43:7 (SAMEKH segs in this stretch: MT 43:10, 43:13, 43:15, single-witness), so the record's rejection of the fold rests entirely on an unstated ground: a defective warrant not alone load-bearing, the seam being carried from the other side by the closing triad and the 43:9 address change (not high; not low, since the strongest rival is left unadjudicated, not merely under-tagged). Medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame opens the row at “Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says:” (web:Isa.43.14), the full title stack spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.14, byte tier) -- a different divine-title pairing than the witness-trial's bare self-declaration at web:Isa.43.11-Isa.43.13. The oracle announces “For your sake, I have sent to Babylon” and closes two verses later on “I am Yahweh, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.” (web:Isa.43.15), just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading keeps this two-verse Redeemer announcement joined to the new-thing oracle that follows as one Babylon-and-exodus complex, since both open on a ‘Yahweh...says’ pattern and share the redemption theme.

current_row.device_notes: The oracle announces judgment on Babylon and the Chaldeans, but its address and rhetorical purpose comfort Israel (‘for your sake’), so the row reads it under the salvation-oracle default rather than as a judgment oracle against a third party; the rival merged reading is disclosed above.

items.claim: The row's only close warrant is an original-language formula claim asserted with no pointed splice and keyed to the translation witness.
items.proposed_change: Splice the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.16 with its tier named as the close warrant, alongside the existing web: reference.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. The shipped close sentence reads 'just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16'; boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.43.16 and no oshb:Isa.43.16, and no splice of that frame stands anywhere in the row; the only other close-side signal cited is the setumah after MT 43:15 (tier-3, single-witness), which cannot warrant a seam alone. The claim itself is byte-true: MT 43:16 is verse-initial כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.43.16, byte tier), a divine-owned frame; the contiguous-skeleton sweep on כה אמר (skeleton tier; count object: skeleton substring, verse count) returns 48 verses book-wide and exactly 4 in chs 41-43 -- MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16 -- so the auditor's digit holds and the 43:15|43:16 seam is sound. The web: keying does not evidence the frame either: WEB 43:16 reads “Yahweh, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters,” (web:Isa.43.16), the English 'says' falling only in the following verse, so the frame is verifiable solely in the MT bytes the row never splices. The row's sole tier-1 close warrant therefore ships outside the mandatory engagement class. Not high (nothing byte-false, no boundary defect); not low (this is the only close warrant, not ancillary disclosure). Medium confirmed; the proposed splice-with-tier repair is the right cure.

items.claim: The strongest-rejected-alternative field records only the rival's own supporting reasons and no ground for rejecting it, on a rival that would merge this span away.
items.proposed_change: Record the refusal in the field: two distinct koh-amar frames stand at oshb:Isa.43.14 and oshb:Isa.43.16, which is what separates the two units rather than joining them.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. The field as shipped is exactly as the auditor describes: rival plus a since-clause, no refusal. But the refusal ground the auditor supplies is already the row's own boundary argument: the row splices its onset frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.14, byte tier) and closes 'just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16', and device_notes states that the merged reading 'is disclosed above'. Bytes: MT 43:14 and MT 43:16 are both verse-initial frames -- כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.16, byte tier) -- both in the divine-frame class, with no frame inside MT 43:15 (the כה אמר skeleton is absent from that verse, skeleton tier), so two frames stand where the rival sees one complex; the rival's own since-clause ('both open on a Yahweh...says pattern') concedes as much. The rival is thus adjudicated by the row, in boundary_rationale rather than in the field, and the field contract (one sentence plus an optional mandated-rival sentence) does not require the refusal there. What remains is a disclosure shortfall: read alone, the field argues for the merge and points to no counter, and the second frame the refusal rests on is unspliced (that is item P12-003#1, not counted twice here). Not a defective warrant in substance, so not medium; not nothing, since the field records only the rival's case. Downgrade to low; the proposed one-clause refusal note is a fair minor repair.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The address reverses at “Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; but you have been weary of me, Israel.” (web:Isa.43.22), spliced at וְלֹא אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב (oshb:Isa.43.22, byte tier) -- a covenant-lawsuit turn to direct singular address, against the seam-adjacent third-person reference to the people that closes the preceding oracle, עַם זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ (oshb:Isa.43.21, byte tier). The legal-dispute vocabulary “Put me in remembrance. Let us plead together. Declare your case, that you may be justified.” (web:Isa.43.26) carries the indictment through to the verdict “Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.” (web:Isa.43.28), just ahead of the fresh fear-not address to “Jacob my servant” that opens web:Isa.44.1.

items.claim: The row's back-seam warrant names a fear-not formula as the onset signal at web:Isa.44.1, but no fear-not formula stands in that verse's bytes in either witness.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: replace 'the fresh fear-not address ... that opens web:Isa.44.1' with the onset signal actually standing in that verse — the adversative-plus-imperative וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier) with its named-servant address — and, if the fear-not is cited at all, locate it at oshb:Isa.44.2 with web:Isa.44.2 added to boundary_evidence_refs.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. MT 44:1 in full is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier): no fear-not stands in it -- the pair skeleton אל תירא is absent from the verse at skeleton tier and no token carries the verb skeleton תירא (skeleton tier) -- and WEB 44:1 reads “Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.” (web:Isa.44.1). The formula stands one verse later, אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.44.2, byte tier); a byte-tier sweep of that exact pointed pair returns 4 verses (MT 37:6, 41:10, 43:1, 44:2; count object: pointed two-token form, verse count), so the auditor's 43:1 identity claim holds at byte tier. The named-servant half of the descriptor is byte-true at 44:1: יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier). The book-order neighbour row places the koh-amar frame and the fear-not it governs 'one verse inside the unit rather than at the onset', so the two rows do locate one formula at two verses. The seam survives without the misplaced formula: the adversative-plus-imperative onset וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier), whose first token matches MT 43:1's וְעַתָּ֞ה (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) at accent-stripped tier only; the verdict close at web:Isa.43.28; and the setumah after MT 43:28 (tier-3, single-witness, confirmed in the inventory). A seam warrant naming a formula at a verse that carries it in neither witness is a defective warrant, not alone load-bearing. Medium confirmed; the proposed relocation repair (onset signal at 44:1, fear-not cited at 44:2 with web:Isa.44.2 added to refs) is byte-sound.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame opens the row at “This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says:” (web:Isa.44.6), a royal-and-Redeemer title stack distinct from the servant address before it, moving into “I am the first, and I am the last” spliced at אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן (oshb:Isa.44.6, byte tier). The witness challenge “Don't fear, neither be afraid...You are my witnesses.” runs to the closing rock-epithet וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier), “I don't know any other Rock.” (web:Isa.44.8) -- the rock epithet, distinct from the adversary and Tyre homographs sharing its skeleton -- just ahead of the idol-maker unit's shift into third-person description that opens web:Isa.44.9.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading extends the row through the idol-maker satire that follows it, reading the combined span as one trial speech in which the satire supplies the witnesses' evidence rather than opening a separate unit.

current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The row's own witness language (‘You are my witnesses’), spliced at וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier), reaches toward the idol-makers' own failed witnesses one verse later (‘their own witnesses don't see, nor know’), spliced at וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier) -- the two forms sharing the same witness root and matching at skeleton tier only, not an identity at byte, nfd, or accent-stripped tier -- a catchword pull toward continuity that the row discloses rather than resolves by merging the two units.

items.claim: The row's cross-seam catchword disclosure labels the two witness forms as matching at skeleton tier only, but they are not identical at skeleton tier.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to device_notes: strike 'and matching at skeleton tier only', state the relation as root-level with containment of the shorter skeleton, and add skeleton to the existing non-identity list alongside byte, nfd and accent-stripped.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the staged consonantal layer. The skeleton of וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) is ואתם עדי and the skeleton of וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier) is ועדיהם המה (both skeleton tier): distinct strings. The witness tokens alone, עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) against וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier), give skeletons עדי and ועדיהם (skeleton tier): distinct, and not identical at accent-stripped tier either; the only relation is that the shorter skeleton is a contiguous substring of the longer -- root sharing with containment. The row's label was tested charitably: a substring collate of the 44:8 token against the whole of MT 44:9 does return skeleton tier, which is presumably how 'matching at skeleton tier' arose, but the row asserts it of 'the two forms', and the two-token run collated against MT 44:9 returns none. The run's own convention treats the identical containment relation as non-identity: the neighbour rows call כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier) against כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) 'not identical at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier' although the shorter skeleton כי גאל is likewise contained in כי גאלתיך (skeleton tier). Under the tier-disclosure standard a recurrence claim's tier label is a byte-checkable claim, and this one overstates, inside a device_notes disclosure that is not load-bearing (the cut rests on the 44:8|44:9 participant shift, and the row discloses the pull rather than acting on it). Medium confirmed; the proposed relabel (root-level with containment; skeleton added to the non-identity list) is correct.

items.claim: The row disambiguates the rock epithet against the adversary and Tyre homographs 'sharing its skeleton', but neither shares that skeleton, and the claim ships without a digit or a named count object.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: either drop the homograph clause, or restate it against the classes that actually share the epithet's skeleton with a digit and count object named, keeping the Tyre and adversary contrast only if labelled a pointed-form contrast rather than a skeleton one.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. The row's own splice וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) carries the rock token צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier), skeleton צור (skeleton tier). Tyre at the head of its oracle is מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.23.1, byte tier), whose name token has the two-consonant skeleton צר (skeleton tier), the same skeleton the adversary/narrow family carries. Neither shares the epithet's skeleton: the two-consonant skeleton is not a contiguous substring of the three-consonant one (nor the reverse), no token of MT 23:1 contains the rock skeleton, and no token of MT 44:8 contains the Tyre skeleton. The contiguous-skeleton sweep on צור (skeleton tier; count object: skeleton substring, verse count) returns 23 verses with no chapter-23 verse among them, and it does include the besieged and fortified forms נְצוּרָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.8, byte tier) and מָצ֑וֹר (oshb:Isa.19.6, byte tier) the auditor names, alongside the plene rock sites MT 17:10, 26:4, 30:29 and 44:8; the sweep on צר (skeleton tier) is a different, pervasive object (133 verses, six of them in ch 23). So 'the adversary and Tyre homographs sharing its skeleton' is byte-false at the tier it names; the hazard catalogue's 'homograph triple' is a sweep-hazard grouping, not a skeleton identity. The digit prong is secondary (the clause is not a universal claim) and does not move severity. The clause is a disambiguation aside: the closing rock epithet is itself byte-true and the close seam rests on the 44:9 participant shift, so the false claim is not load-bearing. Medium confirmed; either proposed repair (drop the clause, or restate it against the classes that do share the skeleton, with a digit) is byte-sound, and the Tyre/adversary contrast survives only as a pointed-form contrast.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The single verse “Sing, you heavens, for Yahweh has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of your trees, for Yahweh has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.” (web:Isa.44.23) is an imperative hymn call to the cosmos, spliced at רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier), set apart from the exhortation before it by its shift from second-person address (‘you are my servant’) to an imperative summons of heavens, earth, and mountains -- a doxology-closure unit for the redemption announcement that precedes it, standing just ahead of the fresh koh-amar self-predication that opens web:Isa.44.24. The petuchah after this verse (oshb:Isa.44.23, single-witness, tier-3) closes the layer's section on the FAR side of the row's own closing seam, grouping Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 with the koh-amar oracle that follows rather than corroborating the isolation argued here; the cut itself rests on the addressee turn, not on that tier-3 layer.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading merges this doxology into the exhortation of Isa.44.21-Isa.44.22 as its closing acclamation rather than isolating it as its own hymn row.
current_row.literature_type_guess: one-verse doxology closing the redemption announcement
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The verse is held as its own isolable doxology-closure unit on the strength of its imperative cosmic-summons form, distinct from both the second-person exhortation before it and the koh-amar self-predication after it. A redeemer catchword straddles both of the row's own seams at root/skeleton level, not as a byte-identical refrain: כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier) before it, the row's own כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier), and גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier, the quoted token standing clear of that verse's ketiv/qere token pair, single-witness apparatus) after it -- a device that argues continuity across both seams without disturbing the cut, which rests on the addressee turn.

items.claim: The row states the location and direction of its tier-3 parashah evidence backwards: the petuchah falls on the row's own closing seam and separates the section from the following oracle, rather than sitting on the far side of that seam and grouping the section with it.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: restate the mark as a petuchah closing the MT 44:21-44:23 section at the row's own closing seam, weak tier-3 corroboration of that seam, while grouping the row's verse with the exhortation before it and so running against the row's front seam; retain the existing disclaimer that the cut rests on the addressee turn.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the mark inventory (MT keys, single witness): SAMEKH at MT 44:20, no mark at MT 44:21 or 44:22, PE at MT 44:23, no mark at MT 44:24, next SAMEKH at MT 44:28. The section that PE closes is therefore MT 44:21-44:23 and its end falls at 44:23|44:24 -- the row's own closing seam for span Isa.44.23-Isa.44.23, not the far side of it -- and that end separates 44:21-23 from the verse-initial frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier; a K/Q verse per the inventory, the splice standing clear of the K/Q pair) rather than grouping them with it. The layer's only pressure runs against the front seam 44:22|44:23, where no mark stands and the section carries across, which is exactly the row's disclosed rival. Both directional claims in the shipped sentence ('on the FAR side of the row's own closing seam'; 'grouping Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 with the koh-amar oracle that follows') are inverted, and the book-order neighbour row states the same PE correctly (section Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 grouping its span with the following doxology). The cut is unaffected: the row rests it on the addressee turn רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) and says the tier-3 layer does not drive it, and the redeemer catchword note stands as shipped. A defective tier-3 mark claim, not alone load-bearing. Medium confirmed; the proposed restatement (PE closing MT 44:21-44:23 at the row's closing seam, weak corroboration of that seam, pressure against the front seam) matches the bytes.
